repo.name: Wiktionary Lookup
repo.description: Offline dictionary for every language in English Wiktionary (via kaikki.org, CC BY-SA 4.0): Chinese built in, 467 languages downloadable in the app. Incremental search by headword, romanization or English.

apps.description:
An offline dictionary built from English Wiktionary. Results update on
every keystroke; search by headword, by romanization (pinyin for Chinese,
with or without tone digits) or by English words in the definitions. Tap a
result to see all of its senses. The speaker button plays the Wiktionary
recording when there is one (from Wikimedia Commons, cached on the device)
and otherwise reads the word with the system text-to-speech voice.

Chinese (about 190,000 entries) ships inside the APK and works without
network access. Every other language that English Wiktionary covers can be
downloaded from the language menu; the indexes are hosted as GitHub release
assets of https://github.com/d33mobile/wiktionary-lookup-data and are kept
on the device after download.

Licensing: the app code is MIT licensed. The dictionary data is derived
from Wiktionary and is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (and GFDL); credit goes
to the Wiktionary contributors (https://en.wiktionary.org/) and to
wiktextract and kaikki.org (https://kaikki.org/dictionary/).

en-US.whatsNew:
- Choose your language on first start; flags (or a script sign) next to every language.
- Entry pages laid out like Wiktionary: pronunciation lines, numbered senses per part of speech with examples, forms, etymology, synonyms and related words, and a link to the Wiktionary page.
- Tap any Chinese character in an entry to look it up; Back steps through the pages you opened.
- Separate icons: the speaker plays a Wiktionary recording and appears only where one exists; text-to-speech has its own but
